prompt_md: You enter a bank with two tellers, both busy, no one else waiting. Service times are random and memoryless, same average for all. Chance you're last of the 3 to leave?
prompt_short: Two busy tellers, you next, memoryless service. Chance you leave last?
hint_md: When a teller frees up, how much head start does the other customer have?
explain_intuition_md: You can't be first out, since you start after someone leaves. At that moment, memoryless service means the other customer's head start counts for nothing: you're both starting fresh. So it's a coin flip who finishes last. 'One of three' gives the tempting third.
explain_math_md: You start when the first teller frees up. Both remaining service times are then exponential with the same rate, so $$P(\text{you leave last}) = P(S_{\text{you}} > S_{\text{other}}) = \tfrac12$$
